name: Carlos March Delgado
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Carlos March Delgado was president of $2.5 billion (net assets) Banca March, Spain's only 100% family-owned bank, for four decades until 2015.
Carlos and his billionaire brother Juan March Delgado are grandchildren of Banca March's founder, Juan March (d. 1962), who started the business in Palma de Mallorca in 1926.
After stepping down as a director of Banca March in 2024, Carlos remains chairman of $5 billion (net assets) investment company Corporación Financiera Alba, which is also nearly 100% family-owned.
Carlos and Juan March Delgado own 69% of Banca March and 42% of Corporación Financiera Alba combined (excluding Banca March's 15% stake in Corporación Financiera Alba).

name: Erman Ilicak
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Erman Ilicak's Ronesans Holding, founded in 1993, operates as construction contractor and real estate developer in 28 countries.
In July 2016, he sold 5% of Ronesans to IFC, a World Bank institution, in a deal that valued the company at $4.3 billion.
Construction firm acquisitions include the Swiss Hergiswill and German Heitcamp in 2013, and the Netherlands' Ballast Nedam in 2015.

In a public-private partnership with the Turkish government, Ronesans has so far built 
healthcare complexes with a contract value of $3.4 billion.
Ronesans is partnering with the Port of Rotterdam to develop the Ceyhan Mega Petrochemical Industrial Zone in the south of Turkey.
forbes_facts: A basketball player during his years at TED high school, Ilicak served as president of the TED Ankara Sports Club from 2014 to 2016.
Ilicak started Ronesans in St. Petersburg, Russia, where he worked as an engineer for billionaire Sinan Tara's construction firm, Enka Insaat ve Sanayi AS.

name: Chan Tan Ching-fen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2022-2025)
forbes_bio: Chan Tan Ching-fen is the wife of the late Hong Kong property tycoon Chan Tseng-hsi. She controls the largest shareholding in Hang Lung Group.
Hang Lung was run by her eldest son, Ronnie, until his retirement in 2024. His son Adriel took over as chairman.
Ronnie's brother Gerald leads the family's Morningside Group, a private equity and venture capital investor.
forbes_facts: Her father Tan Hui-kuk was a second cousin of Sun Yat-sen, the founding father of the Republic of China, and provided Sun with financial support.

name: Remo Ruffini
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Remo Ruffini turned around a nearly bankrupt luxury sportswear firm Moncler, taking the company public in 2013 in one of Italy's largest IPOs in years
Ruffini started out as the company's creative director in 1999 and a few years later bought the brand. Now chairman and CEO, he owns a 15% stake.
Ruffini introduced new colors and designs at Moncler, and partnered with the Carlyle Group to expand internationally.
He got his start in the U.S. working for his father's clothing company, Gianfranco Ruffini.
In 1984 he returned to Italy and founded his own brand, New England Company, which was sold in 2000.
forbes_facts: In December 2021, in Ruffini's first acquisition since taking over, Moncler bought sportswear brand Stone Island in a $1.4 billion cash-and-stock deal.
He owns a 180-foot superyacht, Atlante, as well as a restored chalet in St. Moritz, Switzerland.

name: Hal Jackman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Hal Jackman and his family are the largest shareholders of E-L Financial Corporation, a Toronto investment and insurance holding company.
His father, former Parliament member Harry Jackman, built a financial services empire, which Hal continued to expand over his decades at the helm.
His son, Duncan, now runs the business as chief executive officer, president and chairman of E-L Financial.
Jackman followed in his father's footsteps into politics, serving as the 25th lieutenant governor of Ontario from 1991 to 1997.
forbes_facts: Jackman was chancellor of his alma mater, The University of Toronto, from 1997 to 2003.
Jackman's sister, Nancy Ruth, is Canada's first openly lesbian senator.

name: Hu Kaijun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2012-2026)
forbes_bio: Hu Kaijun is chairman and CEO of China Grand Enterprises, an investment company with interests in healthcare, real estate, agriculture and financial services.
China Grand is the parent of three publicly-traded companies: Grand Pharmaceutical, Huadong Medicine (a wholesaler) and Grand Industrial Holding (a trading business).
Grand Pharmaceutical agreed to buy 87.5% of U.S.-based vascular drug maker BlackSwan Vascular for $37.5 million in 2023.
Hu also wholly owns Beijing Yuanda Huachuang Investment, where he also serves as chairman and CEO.
Hu's wealth is derived primarily from Grand China's stakes in Huadong Medicine and Grand Pharmaceutical.

name: T. Denny Sanford
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: T. Denny Sanford owns First Premier Bank, which specializes in offering credit cards to high-risk borrowers.
The Sioux Falls, South Dakota, bank has just 18 branches, but is one of the largest issuers of Mastercards - many with steep rates and low limits.
An active philanthropist, Sanford says he wants to die broke. To do that he'd have to give away his most valuable asset, First Premier.
Sanford was previously investigated for child pornography after photos of nude underage girls were discovered in his email.
The investigation was closed and charges were never brought. Sanford said his email was hacked.
forbes_facts: Sanford has given more than $1 billion to Sanford Health, a group of 43 nonprofit hospitals formerly called the Sioux Valley Health System.
Sanford's children's education initiatives include one for young boys and girls which he hopes will cut America's divorce rate by 50% in the next 50 years.

name: Ioannis Papalekas
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Ioannis Papalekas is a Greek real estate investor and the largest shareholder of publicly traded investment conglomerate Yoda Group.
Yoda invests in shipping, healthcare, technology and real estate in Cyprus and Greece.
He founded Yoda as a private investment firm in 2019 and took it public on the Cyprus Stock Exchange in 2022; he owns 66% of the shares.
Prior to starting Yoda, he founded office real estate firm Globalworth and took it public on the London Stock Exchange in 2013.
He sold his 13.5% stake in Globalworth, which owns offices in central Europe, for $315 million in early 2020.
forbes_facts: Before starting Globalworth, he developed commercial real estate in Romania, achieving a 175% rate of return for himself and his investors.

name: Wee Ee Lim
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Wee Ee Lim chairs Singapore property development company UOL Group.
He was appointed UOL chairman in 2024 after the death of his father Wee Cho Yaw.
He Joined Haw Par, maker of the popular Tiger Balm ointment, in 1986, and has been serving as its president and CEO since 2003.
In March 2025, the estate of his father, the late Wee Chow Yaw, was transferred to him, his mother and siblings, completing a process that happened over many months.

name: Ajay Jaisinghani
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Ajay Jaisinghani gets his wealth from a minority stake in Polycab India, which makes electrical wires and cables.
Polycab was started as a trading firm in 1986 by his brother Inder Jaisinghani.
The company makes everything from power cables to solar cables to optical fibre cables for the  the power, oil and gas and renewable energy industries.
In 2014, Polycab expanded into products such as electric fans, LED lighting, switches and switchgear.
forbes_facts: The company, which went public in 2019, got a boost in 2022 from increasing electrification and an uptick in spending in the power sector.
Son Bharat sits on Polycab's board.

name: Lawrence Ho
sec_insider_companies: Melco Resorts & Entertainment LTD (MLCO) - Chief Executive Officer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2023); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Lawrence Ho controls Nasdaq-listed casino operator Melco Resorts via Hong Kong-listed Melco International Development.
His partnership with Australian billionaire James Packer, Melco Crown, ended in 2017 after developing four casinos.
Melco Resorts runs three casino-resorts in Macau plus the Mocha chain of slot machine clubs and City of Dreams Manila.
The company has also expanded into Europe, opening in 2023 a $660 million hospital and gaming complex in Cyprus.
EV maker Vinfast, controlled by Vietnam's richest man Pham Nhat Vuong's Vingroup, merged with Ho's Black Spade in a $23 billion SPAC listing on Nasdaq in 2023.
forbes_facts: Ho left investment banking for gaming in 2003, under the license of his late father, casino mogul Stanley Ho, before Melco got a license in 2006.
Lawrence Ho is the oldest living son of the late Macau casino kingpin Stanley Ho, who fathered 17 children by four women.
Melco's origins and name trace to Macau Electric Company, listed on the Hong Kong stock market in 1927.
